A Few Pages of Markdown: Committed AI Configuration and Lower Quality Cost after Coding-Agent Adoption. In Proceedings of the 41st IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE '26), Munich, 12-16 Oct 2026. ACM. https://doi.org/10.1145/3832783.3837546 (arXiv:2608.25241v2)

Stanford University (Denisov-Blanch, Schaeffer, Miranda, Koyejo); Carnegie Mellon University (Agarwal, He, Vasilescu); Grid Dynamics (Azaletskiy)

Evaluates; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — RAMP, a four-level repository AI maturity model and classification pipeline, validated; observational staggered difference-in-differences re-analysis of committed AI configuration as moderator of quality and velocity after coding-agent adoption

No SDD approach. Committed AI configuration artefacts classified by RAMP levels: L1 Unconfigured; L2 Grounded Prompting (context artefacts); L3 Agent-Augmented (capability artefacts); L4 Orchestration (coordination artefacts). Detected for 12 tools (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Aider, AMP, Gemini CLI, Google IDX, JetBrains AI, Kiro, OpenAI Codex, OpenHands) plus cross-tool AGENTS.md, *mcp*.json. Velocity: monthly commits, lines of code added. Adoption dynamics: level transitions, time to next level (Kaplan-Meier), set-and-forget share. Classifier validity: Guttman CR/CS, accuracy and kappa vs human labels

Automatic: RAMP pipeline (file patterns + nomic-embed-text-v1.5 embeddings), git history, SonarQube; staggered DiD (Borusyak imputation estimator) with SEs clustered by repository. Manual: three annotators labelled 195 artefacts from 35 held-out repos

Configurations are maturity strata of treated repositories (agents mixed and not identified per repo; models not stated). Measure: DiD post-adoption change vs propensity-matched non-adopting controls (log outcomes, ≈ % change); no success criterion stated by the authors.
- Matched non-adopter controls (baseline; no agent): reference of the DiD; no separate values reported. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured, no criterion stated by the authors
- L1 (no committed AI configuration) + mixed agents + n.s., agent-first stratum (214 repos): cognitive complexity +52.7% (p<0.001), warnings +24.1% (p<0.01), duplication +15.4% (p<0.05), comment density +7.1% (n.s.); commits +37.6% (p<0.001), lines added +48.1% (p<0.05). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured, no criterion stated by the authors
- L2+ (committed configuration) + mixed agents + n.s., agent-first stratum (182 repos): complexity +26.7% (p<0.01), warnings +14.0% (p<0.05), duplication +14.2% (p<0.01), comments +1.9% (n.s.); commits +27.5% (p<0.001), lines added +68.7% (p<0.001). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured, no criterion stated by the authors
- Four-level gradient (robustness, pooled sample): complexity L1 +54.4%, L2 +39.8% (both p<0.001), L3-L4 indistinguishable from zero; warnings L1 +23.0%, L2 +16.7%, n.s. above; duplication significant only at L1 among L1-L3; L4 duplication +31.4% (p<0.01). L3 and L4 strata small (23 and 40 repos). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors (each level); cost: not measured
- Combined L1-2 (robustness, pooled): complexity +46.6%, warnings +20.9% (both p<0.001). No verdict (re-grouping of the same strata)
- Pooled agent-first + IDE-first (robustness): complexity L1 +54.4% vs L2+ +35.9%; warnings +23.0% vs +20.0%; duplication L1 +16.0% vs L2+ +5.9% (n.s.). No verdict (re-grouping of the same strata)

Observational re-analysis of Agarwal et al.'s staggered DiD panel; treatment = first agent-attributed PR; unit repository-month; propensity-score matched controls; maturity labelled at Nov 2025 snapshot; strata compared within agent-first population. Baseline: L1 stratum and matched non-adopters. Held constant: estimator, outcomes and control pool from Agarwal et al.; prior AI exposure (agent-first). Acceptance tests: N/A. Repetitions: N/A (observational). Human intervention: N/A. Event window 6 months after adoption

L1 shows ~2.0x the complexity increase (+52.7% vs +26.7%) and 1.7x the warnings increase (+24.1% vs +14.0%) of L2+ in the agent-first stratum; duplication similar (1.1x). Velocity rises in both (commits 1.4x higher at L1; lines added higher at L2+). Gap widens over months after adoption. Within-stratum effects significant; formal test of the difference between strata Not reported. Adoption: 73.8% of artefacts committed once and never modified; 95.9% enter at L2; no reversals

Partly: stratification separated quality trajectories, robust across groupings; contrast identified only within agent-first (IDE-first L1 only 22 repos); warnings weakly identified (pre-trends). Classifier reproduced human repo-level labels for 34/35 repos (kappa_w 0.829). Limitations stated: observational, model capability and usage intensity unobserved, reverse causality, shared control pool, presence not quality of artefacts

Associations hypothesis-generating, not causal; model capability and AI usage intensity confounders; maturity measured at end snapshot (only 3.8% of agent-first L2+ committed configuration before adoption); SonarQube proxies; presence not content quality of artefacts; L4 absent in development sample; 6-month and 14-month windows; governance outside the repo invisible. Future: content specificity and upkeep, subsystem-level measurement, designs fixing configuration before adoption
